title.narrative: Improved labour inspection and OSH in the Occuppied Palestinian Territories in line with the International Labour Standards and human rights

description.narrative: In recent years, the Occupied Palestinian Territory made substantial progress in strengthening the labour inspection and occupational safety and health (OSH) framework with the support of ILO. Key milestones include the finalization of the draft National Labour Inspection and OSH Policy, which serves as a blueprint for reforming and enhancing the role and effectiveness of labour inspection across the territory. Building on this foundation, the ILO aims to develop and implement a gender-responsive OSH policy and program. This initiative will be spearheaded by the national tripartite OSH committee and is expected to receive endorsement from the council of ministers. The gender-responsive OSH policy and program aim to identify and mitigate risks disproportionately affecting women in the workplace, promote inclusive participation, and enhance access to resources and support. This targeted approach aims to improve workplace safety and health, while also addressing gender disparities in occupational risks and protections. This, in turn, will lead to improved compliance with international labour standards and human rights in labour inspection and OSH, a more effective system focusing on gender-specific needs and strengthened institutional capacity among national tripartite partners to foster a safety and health culture.
